newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-BEN HOLLIOAKE STARS AS ENGLAND SWEEP ONE-DAYERS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BEN HOLLIOAKE STARS AS ENGLAND SWEEP ONE-DAYERS.

text.p: Ben Hollioake, who had never set foot inside Lord's until Sunday, marked his England debut at cricket's traditional headquarters with a compelling 63 off 48 balls as Australia lost the one-day series 3-0.

All-rounder Hollioake, born in Australia but educated in England, Alec Stewart, who hit 79, and John Crawley, with 52, spurred their side to a six-wicket victory with one over to spare in the third and final international.

Australia, put in to bat, scored 269 all out in 49.2 of their 50 overs, thanks mainly to a fluent 95 from 96 deliveries by Mark Waugh, and England eased home at 270 for four to follow six-wicket wins in each of the first two games.

Hollioake, who is the younger brother of Surrey and England team mate Adam, named England's man of the series, played a refreshingly uninhibited innings with style and confidence after coming in at number three when captain Mike Atherton was out for one in the sixth over.
A straight driven four off Glenn McGrath was Hollioake's first scoring shot, which he repeated in the paceman's next over, and he subsequently struck the same bowler for three fours in another over.

Hollioake then attacked the wrist spin of Shane Warne, whom he straight drove for four and struck for six over mid-wicket, having completed his half-century in 37 balls. He was out when he cut Jason Gillespie uppishly to Steve Waugh at backward point, and departed to a standing ovation.
"I was a bit surprised to be playing today, but it was quite a good day to step inside Lord's for the first time. It was brilliant, I loved it," said Hollioake.
"I was not as nervous as I thought I would be, though still a bit nervous. In the end, I was annoyed at getting out because I thought I had a chance of going on for three figures."

After Hollioake's dismissal, his Surrey team mate Stewart played some characteristically well-timed strokes to make his 79 off 106 balls which, allied to Crawley's 52 in 68 deliveries, ensured there was no way back into the game for Australia.
Atherton said: "It has been a terrific week for us. Our attitude was important today. It was vital we drove home our advantage and that is what we did."
Australia's uneven innings had been dominted by Mark Waugh's elegant strokeplay, the New South Wales batsman driving and cutting handsomely as he completed his half-century in exactly 50 deliveries.

Waugh shared a second-wicket stand of 50 in seven overs with twin brother Steve (17) and put on 79 for the fourth wicket with Justin Langer (29) as the touring team battled to wrest the initiative which Darren Gough had given to England in his new-ball spell.

The Yorkshire pace bowler captured three for 27 in his first six overs by dispatching one-day international debutant Matthew Elliott for one, Steve Waugh and Michael Bevan (8), who came into the match with an average of 57.69 in limited overs games for Australia.

Gough, whose consistently controlled bowling has been a key element in England's series win, subsequently took the important wicket of Mark Waugh, who had hit 12 fours when he was trapped lbw in the 33rd over. Gough also dismissed Jason Gillespie to finish with a haul of five for 44.

Adam Gilchrist (33) and wicketkeeper Ian Healy (27) added useful middle order runs and Mike Kasprowicz provided a tail-end flourish by hammering an unbeaten 28 in 26 balls to give their side a relatively competitive total.
